label: copy-phase input n (fed-back n at original position >= 2)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, at steps where the fed-back input token is n (the model just output an n) and that n is original token 2 or later (recall_idx >= 3). It never fires during the original phase or at the delimiter, even when n is input there, and essentially never on any other input token. When the fed-back n was original token 1 (recall_idx 2) it fires rarely and weakly. Magnitude rises with how deep into the sequence the n sits: n at original positions 1-3 gives about 0.1-0.5 of max, and n at positions 5-7 gives about 0.9-1.0. When two n tokens come back to back, the second one fires a bit less (about 0.7 of the first). Activation does not depend on the output token, the previous tokens, or the first token.

issues: The structural claims hold. The original phase and the delimiter have 0 active steps, and (phase==0)&(in_tok==n) has precision 0 over 107k steps. Inputs other than n account for about 55 active steps out of 57.8k.

Misses (996 test steps, 0.2% of activation mass) are all copy-phase n at recall_idx 2, firing weakly (0.03-0.15 of max). This matches the stated caveat. Widening the predicate to recall_idx>=2 drops precision to 0.78 (F1 0.876), so leaving that cell out is correct.

False positives (673 test steps) all fall at recall_idx==3: the fed-back n is original token 2 and the feature does not fire. Precision in that cell is 0.958 overall, 0.996 for L<=5 and 0.965 for L=9. It is a mild, L-dependent weak edge at the low end of the position ramp, not a separate pattern. At recall_idx>=4, precision is 1.000.
The label says 'original position >= 2', which matches the predicate's recall_idx>=3, so the label does not overclaim.

The magnitude claims could only be checked indirectly. Mass share per active step rises from recall_idx 3 to 5+, which supports a ramp with position. The back-to-back claim (second n at about 0.7 of the first) is not supported by the examples. In 'i n n n', the first n (recall_idx 2) fires at 0.04 and the second at 0.33, because position dominates. In 'e n n b' it is 0.10 then 0.17. These are minor descriptive issues, not predicate failures.
